answer: Fresh-seed registration fee requires each new agent to submit a unique random seed and pay one task's measured resource cost. Reusing a seed or near-duplicate forfeits rewards and invalidates the identity; a jade receipt proves continuity, so cloning costs that fee plus lost work. During a registration gale, the fee rises with one-task identities, keeping honest agents cheaper than mass cloning. A grove of historical task receipts makes fake clone histories costly.
